title: Export Adapter: Customer Acceptance Tests & Onboarding Checklist
content:
Purpose:
This document captures the acceptance tests, minimal customer requirements, and operational checks that must be completed for a Redwood export adapter to be accepted for production integration with customer SIEMs (Splunk HEC, Datadog Logs HTTP API, Azure Sentinel / Log Analytics). It combines contract expectations (field-level), RBAC and audit requirements, and evidence automation hooks required for compliance reviews.

Scope and goals:
- Define a deterministic set of acceptance test cases for on-prem / cloud export adapters.
- Provide clear mapping of Redwood audit log schema -> SIEM envelope examples for three target sinks.
- Call out RBAC v2 permissions and evidence automation endpoints that customers and SREs rely on for SOC audits.
- Give a checklist for handoff to Solutions Engineering and Customer Success.

Audience:
- Security & Compliance, Solutions Eng, Customer Success, SRE, Customer SOC engineers.

Prerequisites before starting acceptance testing:
1) Customer has provided destination endpoint(s): Splunk HEC token+endpoint, Datadog API key+endpoint, or Sentinel workspace ID+key.
2) Network egress rules validated (TLS, IP allowlist if present).
3) RBAC role created for export service account per RBAC v2: roles/telemetry-exporter.read, roles/telemetry-exporter.send.
4) Onboarding ticket created and linked (see linked_artifacts).

Minimal data contract (fields that must be present in each exported event):
- event_id (string, uuid)
- timestamp (ISO-8601 UTC)
- tenant_id (string) — pseudonymous if customer requires tenant mapping obfuscation
- product_area (string) — e.g., inference, auth, billing
- model_id (string) — model.alias or model.version used to serve request
- route (string) — Redwood API route / endpoint name
- request_tokens (int) — request token count
- response_tokens (int) — response token count
- latency_ms (int) — end-to-end time for request handling in ms
- outcome (string) — success | partial | failed
- error_code (string) — if outcome != success
- pii_redacted (boolean) — true if PII detected and redacted before export
- raw_payload_present (boolean) — true only when customer has explicitly approved raw copies
- sample_hash (string) — optional deterministic hash for content reconcilation without sharing content

Audit log mapping notes:
- Redwood maintains an internal audit-activity record (audit_event) for each exported record. Acceptance requires that for every exported SIEM event there exists an audit_event in Redwood that contains at minimum: actor_id, action, target, timestamp, request_id.
- Audit_event IDs must be correlated with event_id in the exported envelope via audit_event_id field when possible.

Evidence automation hooks (what SRE must provide to satisfy SOC evidence requests):
- Evidence API endpoint: GET /evidence/export/{export_id}?from=...&to=... (returns signed artifact pointer list).
- On acceptance, export adapter must register evidence hooks that emit a small metadata bundle for each batch: {export_id, batch_start, batch_end, count, sha256(manifest)}. Redwood will archive manifests to the compliance bucket with retention metadata.
- Evidence manifests must include redaction decisions per record (if any) and link to the audit_event_id.

SIEM envelope examples (acceptance tests validate structure and transformations):
1) Splunk HEC (event payload example):
{
  "time": "2026-01-15T18:23:45.123Z",
  "host": "redwood-exporter-01",
  "source": "redwood.inference/export",
  "sourcetype": "redwood:telemetry:event",
  "event": {
    "event_id": "8f14e45f-ce4a-4b3a-9a9e-1b2c3d4f5a6b",
    "tenant_id": "cust-12345",
    "product_area": "inference",
    "model_id": "gptq-6b-v2",
    "route": "/v1/generate",
    "request_tokens": 32,
    "response_tokens": 118,
    "latency_ms": 142,
    "outcome": "success",
    "pii_redacted": true,
    "audit_event_id": "audit-20260115-0001"
  }
}

2) Datadog Logs HTTP API (single JSON line expected for POST):
{
  "ddsource": "redwood-exporter",
  "service": "redwood-inference",
  "host": "exporter-prod-us-west",
  "message": "redwood telemetry event",
  "timestamp": 1705430625.123,
  "attributes": {
    "event_id": "8f14e45f-ce4a-4b3a-9a9e-1b2c3d4f5a6b",
    "tenant_id": "cust-12345",
    "model_id": "gptq-6b-v2",
    "latency_ms": 142,
    "outcome": "success",
    "pii_redacted": true
  }
}

3) Azure Sentinel / Log Analytics (LogEntry example via Data Collector API):
{
  "TimeGenerated": "2026-01-15T18:23:45.123Z",
  "Computer": "redwood-exporter-01",
  "EventOrigin": "redwood.inference",
  "EventType": "TelemetryEvent",
  "EventData": {
    "event_id": "8f14e45f-ce4a-4b3a-9a9e-1b2c3d4f5a6b",
    "tenant_id": "cust-12345",
    "route": "/v1/generate",
    "request_tokens": 32,
    "response_tokens": 118,
    "latency_ms": 142,
    "outcome": "success"
  }
}

Acceptance test matrix (must pass all rows to sign-off):
- Connectivity tests:
  - A1: Verify HEC endpoint reachable over TLS and token accepted (status 200).
  - A2: Verify Datadog API key accepted and endpoint returns 202 for batched events.
  - A3: Verify Sentinel workspace key accepted and response 200 for data collector ingestion.
- Contract tests (field level):
  - B1: All minimal data contract fields present for 100% of sampled events (sample size: 500 or 1 hour, whichever is larger).
  - B2: PII redaction flag set whenever redaction step executed; random sample verify no raw PII exported.
- Latency and retry behavior:
  - C1: End-to-end export latency from Redwood export queue to SIEM ingest <= 5s median for small batches during normal load.
  - C2: Exponential-backoff retry observed on 429/5xx with jitter; no silent data loss for transient errors.
- Volume and rate limiting tests:
  - D1: Adapter must respect customer-side bandwidth caps and Redwood-configured per-tenant QPS.
  - D2: Thundering herd test: 10k events/sec injected across 10 tenants; adapter degrades gracefully and emits backpressure metrics.
- Evidence automation and audit correlation:
  - E1: For any exported batch, an evidence manifest is created and stored; API returns manifest pointer and digest.
  - E2: For sampled exported events (n=50), audit_event entries exist and correlate to export events by audit_event_id.

RBAC v2 requirements (minimum):
- role: telemetry-exporter.send — allows service account to POST to configured external endpoints and read export configs.
- role: telemetry-exporter.read — read-only, used by Solutions Eng for troubleshooting (no ability to change endpoints).
- role: telemetry-audit.view — ability to access audit_event objects for evidence correlation.
- All roles must require MFA and be bound to service principals for automation. Acceptance requires screenshots or IAM bindings exported as evidence.

Onboarding checklist (tick boxes expected in ticket before sign-off):
- [ ] Destination details provided and validated (endpoint, token/key, IP allowlist).
- [ ] RBAC roles provisioned and confirmed.
- [ ] Sample exports ingested into customer SIEM and visible in LRM dashboards.
- [ ] Evidence manifests created for initial test window and accessible to customer security.
- [ ] PII policy reviewed and redaction toggles set per tenant.
- [ ] Rate limit profile agreed (burst QPS and sustained QPS).
- [ ] Run acceptance test matrix and attach results CSV to ticket.
- [ ] Customer SOC signs off on contract mapping and retention behavior.

Failure modes & remediation guidance (operational notes):
- Failure: HEC token rotated unexpectedly -> adapter should mark endpoint as error, queue events to local durable store and notify SRE/CS.
  - Remediation: rotate token in system, run replay for queued batches, mark ticket resolved when backlog drained.
- Failure: Sink rate limiting -> adapter should buffer with backpressure signals; if buffer > threshold, drop oldest non-critical debug events and mark dropped_count in manifests.
- Failure: Evidence manifest mismatch -> trigger forensics pipeline: collect manifest, corresponding audit_events, and raw batch; escalate to Security for analysis.

Performance knobs & configuration suggestions (for Solutions Eng):
- Batch window: 50–200 events or 100–500ms based on latency SLOs.
- Retry policy: base=200ms, multiplier=2, max_backoff=60s, max_retries=8, jitter=0.2.
- Redaction pipeline: adaptive PII detector + deterministic hashing for accepted sample_hash values.

Sign-off criteria (must be explicit in ticket):
- All acceptance matrix checks show PASS.
- Evidence manifests available and API returns valid pointers.
- Customer confirms logs are arriving in their SIEM with required fields for 24 hours.
- Security approves RBAC bindings and retention/PII policy.

Appendix: quick troubleshooting commands and queries:
- Splunk search to validate events: index=* sourcetype="redwood:telemetry:event" | stats count by model_id, outcome
- Datadog log query: @service:redwood-inference AND @attributes.event_id:8f14e45f*
- Sentinel Kusto: RedwwodTelemetryEvent | where TimeGenerated > ago(1h) | summarize count() by EventType

Owner / contact: Asha Patel (security-and-compliance) — asha.patel@redwood.ai
Review history:
- 2025-11-05: initial draft by Asha Patel
- 2026-01-20: added evidence automation hooks (Diego Morales)
- 2026-02-20: updated SIEM examples and sign-off checklist (Lina Zhou)

Notes / open questions to resolve during onboarding:
- Should we support per-tenant field-level allowlist for raw_payload_export? (Action: Solutions Eng + Legal decision)
- Level of sampling for audit correlation for high QPS tenants (default 1/1000).

End of document.
